hypothesis: Decomposition into raw English sub-queries (Direction 4/5) still leaves a query-document distribution gap: the user's words don't match the tool catalog's intent_phrase distribution. If the decomposer LLM emits one hypothetical tool description per step (in the same shape as our enrichment intent_phrase), the embedded query lands directly in the corpus's distribution - matching tools by description-to-description similarity rather than colloquial-query-to-description similarity. Best for implicit/under-specified steps the user didn't spell out (e.g. 'audit log' implies get_current_datetime).

papers.title: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels (HyDE)
papers.key_claim: An LLM generates a hypothetical document answering the query; embedding the hypothetical document instead of the raw query closes the unsupervised query-document distribution gap. Beats Contriever zero-shot, comparable to fine-tuned retrievers across web search / QA / fact verification.

papers.title: Query2doc: Query Expansion with Large Language Models
papers.key_claim: Concatenating an LLM-generated pseudo-document with the original query lifts BM25 by 3-15% on MS-MARCO/TREC DL and improves SOTA dense retrievers in- and out-of-domain - confirming corpus-distribution alignment is the lever.

baseline.miss_breakdown: Implicit-step misses are well represented: 'check today's date for the audit log' -> get_current_datetime, 'pull my loyalty card transactions and total them up' -> calculator. Both are sub-steps the user does not name explicitly.

design.prompt: Single LLM call. System: 'For each step in this query, write a one-sentence description of the tool that would solve it - phrased like a tool catalog entry. Catalog covers L1 domains: {L1_titles_and_one_line_descriptions}. Output JSON list of strings.' User: original query.
design.retrieval: For each hypothetical description h_i: h_emb = embed(h_i); candidates_i = retrieve(tree, h_emb, ...) -> rerank. Union via max-score-per-tool fusion (same as D4/D5).
design.key_difference_vs_d4: The embedded query for retrieval is the LLM's hypothetical *tool description*, not a rephrased *user sub-query*. Aligns embedding-space match with the corpus's own intent_phrase distribution.
files_to_touch: src/tool_index/retrieval/decompose.py - hyde_decompose(query, llm, l1_descriptions) -> list[str] (descriptions, not queries)
Optional: also try Query2Doc variant - concat hypothetical description with original sub-query before embedding

measurement.metric: complex set-recall@10, complex full-cover, simple recall@10
ablation: Direction 6 (decompose to hypothetical tool descriptions) - this direction
Direction 6 + Query2Doc (concat hypothetical with original sub-query)
measurement.success_threshold: complex set-recall@10 >= 0.92 AND simple recall@10 >= 0.97 AND latency overhead <= 2x baseline

risks: LLM hallucinates capabilities the catalog does not have -> hypothetical description embeds far from any real tool -> noise. Mitigated by L1 schema in prompt (LLM can only invent within listed domains).
Single hypothetical description per step may be too narrow - one tool can have multiple phrasings. Consider emitting 2-3 hypothetical descriptions per step and max-fusing.
Cost: LLM tokens scale with number of steps in the query; longer queries get more expensive.
decision_rule: Promote if complex set-recall@10 >= 0.92 AND simple recall@10 >= 0.97. If D6 beats D4 by >= 0.04 it justifies the extra prompt complexity; otherwise prefer the simpler D4/D5.
